A.name: same_artist_similar_style
A.expected_relationship: A coherent City Girl cluster: mellow lo-fi instrumentals with closely related texture, pacing, and production.

tracks.rationale: Dreamy instrumental lo-fi from the Loveless Shadows era; a direct positive control for City Girl's soft, sample-rich sound.
Warm, relaxed Snow Rose instrumental chosen to match the group's intimate beat-driven production.
Another gentle Snow Rose cut with the same understated lo-fi palette and energy.
Airy, reflective Snow Rose instrumental expected to remain close to the other City Girl controls.
Short ambient-leaning City Girl piece that preserves the core lo-fi palette while adding modest textural variation.

B.name: same_artist_stylistically_varied
B.expected_relationship: Shared LE SSERAFIM voices and pop production should remain visible, but the softer R&B, disco-pop, warm midtempo, western-funk, and dark electronic cuts should not collapse into a uniformly tight cluster.

tracks.rationale: Warm midtempo pop chosen as the gentler end of the artist's production range.
Sleek disco-funk production provides a rhythmic contrast to the quieter selections.
Sparse, soft R&B-influenced track tests whether sonic style outweighs shared vocal identity.
High-energy western-funk pop with Nile Rodgers creates an intentionally strong production contrast.
Dark, minimal electronic production represents a different recent-era texture and energy.

C.name: lofi_chillhop_different_artists
C.expected_relationship: Cross-artist lo-fi/chillhop tracks should cluster through soft drums, mellow samples, restrained dynamics, and hazy texture rather than artist identity.

tracks.rationale: Mellow, atmospheric lo-fi beat selected as a central cross-artist style reference.
Compact sample-driven chillhop with a historically SAFE rank-3 recovery.
Warm jazz-inflected lo-fi production should connect through groove and instrumentation.
Soft, nostalgic lo-fi beat broadens the cluster without changing its core sonic character.
Dusty vocal-sample lo-fi adds modest vocal texture while retaining the same beat aesthetic.

D.name: rhythmic_korean_pop_different_artists
D.expected_relationship: Rhythmic, polished Korean pop and pop-rap productions should form a second cross-artist cluster that is audibly distinct from the mellow lo-fi Group C.

tracks.rationale: Hard-edged electronic dance-pop anchors the energetic end of the cluster.
Rhythmic pop-rap with a historically SAFE rank-2 selection adds groove-led variety.
Minimal electropop/R&B production tests cross-artist similarity within polished Korean pop.
Percussive contemporary idol pop/hip-hop reinforces the cluster's dense rhythmic production.
Dramatic synth-pop and rock texture supplies a SAFE rank-3 recovery and controlled stylistic breadth.

E.name: heterogeneous_negative_control
E.expected_relationship: These acoustic pop, distorted electronic, melodic rap, solo piano, and orchestral ballad tracks should have lower and more varied mutual similarities than the positive-control clusters.

tracks.rationale: Intimate acoustic singer-songwriter pop is unlike the electronic and instrumental controls.
Distorted, high-energy electronic production supplies a strong negative contrast.
Melodic rap introduces prominent rap delivery and trap production.
Solo-piano video-game arrangement is intentionally sparse and instrumental.
Large orchestral K-drama ballad provides the negative set's vocal and cinematic extreme.
